Subject: GPU commitment tranches and activation windows — HarborSight deal

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the productive demo yesterday. As requested, attached is a concise proposal that lays out three reservation structures for HarborSight to consider. High-level options: 

1) Progressive Tranche (recommended for predictable growth)
   - Initial cluster: 32 A100-equivalent GPUs
   - Minimum guaranteed: 16 GPUs after month 6 (grace activation)
   - Ramp: +16 GPUs at month 3, +16 GPUs at month 9 based on usage thresholds
   - Pricing: blended rate with 12-month commitment and step-up credits

2) Flat Baseline + Burst Pool (cost-savvy, flexible)
   - Baseline cluster: 24 GPUs always available
   - Burst pool: 24 GPUs shared across region with higher per-token rate when used
   - Ramp: baseline can be increased at quarter boundaries with 30-day notice

3) Stepped Long-Term Commit (lower unit cost, longer lead-time)
   - Commit to 64 GPUs over 24 months with front-loaded activation windows (first 32 active month 1, remaining active month 7)
   - Built-in optionality: one 90-day deferral on second activation for seasonality

Attached: summary PDF and a commitment table that maps months to active GPU counts and estimated burn.

Two asks for you: 1) which of the three aligns best with your Q4 product roadmap; 2) confirm procurement timing (do you need a PO by Oct 20 to hit a Nov activation?).

I can walk through the numbers in a short call if helpful — available Mon/Tue afternoon PT.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: HarborSight_Commitment_Tranches_v1.pdf, HS-088-commitment-table.xlsx
From: Alex Ramirez <alex@harborsight.ai>

Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 12:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GPU commitment tranches and activation windows — HarborSight deal

Hi Priya —

Appreciate the clear options. Quick reactions from our side:

- Progressive Tranche looks appealing since we expect staged feature launches and can align activations to release milestones.
- The deferability on the stepped long-term commit (90 days) is helpful for our planning — can that be extended to 120 days for the second activation?
- Procurement: we aim to confirm budgets by Oct 18 but cannot sign long-term license terms without legal review (likely 2–3 weeks).

Two constraints: Marina will need explicit SLAs around peak-day latency for the burst pool if we touch that option; and we need visibility into cost per 1M tokens for the different activation states (16/32/48/64 GPUs active).

Can we do a 30 minute call next Tue (Oct 6) to walk the numbers and the SLA language?

Thanks,
Alex
VP Product, HarborSight
Alex@harborsight.ai

Priya — quick answers below, happy to refine before the Tue call.

1) Extending the deferral window to 120 days: operationally OK if we tie it to a one-time scheduling fee (to reserve capacity) — recommend a $15k scheduling fee for the deferred activation and an option to convert fee against committed spend if they complete activation within 120 days.

2) Provisional soft-start for first tranche (30 days): feasible. Offer a provisional activation with a 30-day trial period billed at 60% of the committed rate (credits applied to the first full invoice if they sign within 60 days). This keeps runway without full contract exposure.

3) Burst pool SLA wording (draft): "Burst pool availability at 99.5% monthly, and 95th-percentile token-latency target for peak-day workloads under 450ms for the specified model family. When burst pool is used, token pricing increases by 35% over baseline committed rate."

4) Cost-per-1M-token estimates: attached commit table includes modeled unit costs for expected utilization tiers (16/32/48/64 GPUs). I'll update numbers for their specific model family on the Tue call.

I'll prepare an editable term-sheet with the scheduling fee, provisional-start language, and the SLA snippet for us to share on the call.

-Ben
